The execution trace accordingly shows "no off-route segment exists" and the only allowed outcome is no_action.

The refund formula in RD-2 also yields zero. This is a RydeTAXI trip, so any refund would be Σ(unexempted extra_km) × per-km rate; with extra_km = 0 (8.9 km optimal vs 8.8 km actual) the sum is 0.0 km, and 0 km × rate = $0.00 [F1][F3][RD-2]. The trip was also shorter in time than quoted — 13.3 min vs 16 min estimated (−3.0 min) [F2] — which is inconsistent with a longer reroute [F2][RD-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute as unfounded; no fare adjustment and no account action — the metered RydeTAXI fare of $21.26 stands.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider filed a route-deviation complaint ("the driver must have taken a longer route"), but the system records do not support it. Actual distance was 8.8 km against an optimal route of 8.9 km, i.e. −0.1 km (−1%) [F1], and the fare record confirms the billed distance of 8.8 km did not exceed the optimal route of 8.9 km [F3]. Under RD-1, a deviation requires an off-route segment with extra kilometres; no such segment is measured here, so no unexempted detour exists [F1][F3][RD-1]. The execution trace accordingly shows "no off-route segment exists" and the only allowed outcome is no_action.

The refund formula in RD-2 also yields zero. This is a RydeTAXI trip, so any refund would be Σ(unexempted extra_km) × per-km rate; with extra_km = 0 (8.9 km optimal vs 8.8 km actual) the sum is 0.0 km, and 0 km × rate = $0.00 [F1][F3][RD-2]. The trip was also shorter in time than quoted — 13.3 min vs 16 min estimated (−3.0 min) [F2] — which is inconsistent with a longer reroute [F2][RD-1].

The charged total is fully accounted for by metered components: base $3.90 + distance $12.42 (8.8 km) + time $3.47 (13.3 min) + platform $1.47 + waiting $0.00, with surge 1.0× and no discount, summing to $21.26 [F4][F5][FARE-1]. Check: 3.90 + 12.42 + 3.47 + 0.00 + 1.47 = $21.26 [F5][RD-2]. No unpublished or unexplained add-on appears, so FARE-1 is not breached [F4][F5][FARE-1].

The rider's "heavy rain / slow trip" explanation is weather-related, not route-related: heavy rain of 18.5 mm is recorded [F12], while the speed bands on Pan Island Expressway and Airport Boulevard were 40–49 km/h, i.e. band 5, which is far from the band 1–2 congestion range, and in any event RD-4(b) alone cannot exempt a segment [F9][F10][RD-4]. No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the window [F11], and since no segment is off-route, no RD-4 justification is needed at all [F11][RD-4].

The driver's statement that he followed the app route [F8] is consistent with, not contradicted by, the gps and fare records [F1][F3], so nothing turns on it either way under RD-1.

Finally, RD-6's account-action condition is not met: flag_account requires an upheld deviation (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) AND a 90-day upheld-route-dispute count ≥ 1; here the case is not upheld, and the driver shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld across 1081 trips in 90 days [F14][RD-6]. No flag is warranted.

Because no segment added extra kilometres, the RD-2 refund amount for an unexempted detour is zero, so the metered total of $21.26 (base $3.90, distance $12.42 for 8.8 km, time $3.47 for 13.3 min, platform $1.47) may be recorded as compliant and no mileage refund is due.

weaknesses: The rider's own perception of overcharging rests only on the complaint wording; the system records F1 and F3 directly contradict it (actual 8.8 km vs optimal 8.9 km; billed distance not in excess), and under the rules the system records win over statements.

The rider could argue that heavy rain and slow traffic (F9, F10, F12) made the metered fare feel high, but RD-4 only excuses a reroute when supported by a traffic incident on the replaced optimal route; F11 shows no incident, and RD-2 requires actual extra kilometres for any refund, which F1/F3 show do not exist.
